original_text:
Expedia Group Interview Experience.
Compensation Range: 35+ LPA
Role: Data Engineer
Application Method: Referral

𝟭𝘀𝘁 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 – 𝗛𝗶𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗿 (𝗘𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱)

- Deep dive into project architecture
- Heavy focus on streaming systems – recurring theme at Expedia
- Advanced discussion on:
 Kafka: Backpressure, design challenges
- Database internals: Indexing, partitioning, connection pooling
- Strong emphasis on fundamentals and system-level thinking

𝟮𝗻𝗱 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 – 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 + 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘀

- Extensive discussion on: Microservices: APIs, JWT, SAML authentication
- Spark Internals: Execution plan, memory, transformations/actions
- At least 25–30 technical questions asked
- Focus aligned with resume content (e.g., microservices, Spark)

𝟯𝗿𝗱 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 – 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 + 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴

- Started with programming (tricky array-based problem)
- Follow-up: Design a streaming system end-to-end
- Topics:
 Kafka, Spark Streaming
 Expectations to know Flink (optional)
 Real-time data design and processing focus

𝟰𝘁𝗵 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 – 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁 & 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁

- End-to-end data pipeline implementation
- SDLC process: From requirement to deployment
- Behavioral Questions (STAR format):
 Team conflict resolution
 Role models, ownership, communication

Interview referance - https://lnkd.in/gyYztWrH

If you are preparing for Data Engineering interviews then you should check my personally crafted Interview Experiences for 100+ Companies

𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗸 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗞𝗜𝗧 - https://lnkd.in/giY6RZu2
𝗖𝗼𝘂𝗽𝗼𝗻 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 - DATA10 to get 10% discount.

If you've read so far, do LIKE and RESHARE the post👍

ai_analysis.summary: The source is a concise, high-level interview-experience outline for an Expedia Group Data Engineer role, with referral as the application method and a listed compensation range of 35+ LPA. It describes four rounds: a hiring-manager round focused on project architecture, recurring streaming-system themes, Kafka backpressure and design challenges, database internals, fundamentals, and system-level thinking; a data-engineering and Spark round covering microservices, APIs, JWT and SAML authentication, Spark execution plans, memory, transformations/actions, and resume-aligned questioning; a system-design and programming round with a tricky array-based problem, an end-to-end streaming-system design, Kafka and Spark Streaming listed as topics, optional Flink knowledge, and a real-time data focus; and a final HR/staffing round covering end-to-end data-pipeline implementation, the SDLC from requirement to deployment, and STAR-format behavioral questions. The post states that the second round included at least 25–30 technical questions but does not provide detailed technical answers, implementation steps, or the array problem itself.
